Stale — disclosure already present in memory.rs:94-133. The module-level rustdoc carries a dedicated '# Single-user limitation (per-caller scoping is NOT implemented)' heading that walks all three of the bead's missing-disclosure items:

1. Per-user uniqueness scoping (memory.rs:102-109) — names find_uniqueness_conflict and the multi-user-rejection failure mode explicitly.
2. isPrivate visibility scoping (memory.rs:110-115) — cites the workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' rule and states 'every caller sees every private record in the account'.
3. principal_id default (memory.rs:128-133) — states the impl inherits the foundation default returning None, and that contributors copying into a multi-user backend MUST add the principal_id wiring.

The 'What a real backend MUST do' subsection at memory.rs:117-126 provides the action-side counterpart with a numbered list. The disclosure is more comprehensive than the bead's suggested 'CARGO-CULT WARNING' framing — it tells the reader what to do, not just what not to do.

find_uniqueness_conflict itself also carries an inline 'Single-user limitation' rustdoc at memory.rs:537-548 (closing also bd:JMAP-ayoz.10's separate warning, now adjacent to the new NOT A PRODUCTION PATTERN block).

No further code or doc change warranted. Closing as duplicate-of-already-done.
title: MemoryBackend rustdoc fails to disclose single-user limitations on uniqueness / isPrivate / principal_id
